title: Full AES-192 four-related-key amplified-boomerang recovery, 2009 conference version

target.description: Standard full 12-round AES-192 and its actual key schedule, under four key-schedule-induced related secret keys.

setting.key_relation: Let H_i map a master key to its192-bit expanded-key state K^i. KB=H_1^-1(H_1(KA) XOR DeltaK1); KC=H_4^-1(H_4(KA) XOR NablaK4); KD=H_4^-1(H_4(KB) XOR NablaK4), using Table5. These are not generally fixed-XOR master-key offsets.
setting.key_population: no weak-key restriction reported; arbitrary target-key construction (editorial interpretation)
setting.plaintext_model: chosen plaintext structures under four related keys
assumptions: The attacker can obtain encryptions under the four key relations in Section 6.1.
Section 6.2 uses encryption access followed by offline quartet processing; a decryption oracle is not required by that algorithm.
The source presents only a brief ranking analysis and explicitly defers full details to its extended version. Reading this conference edition does not authenticate unpublished/extended details.

time.note: Section 6.2 final estimate; not normalized to an exact count of full AES encryptions.

data.note: Four keys times 2^73 structures times 2^48 plaintexts; conference version only.

memory.note: Table1 PDF2 reports2^152. Section6.2 PDF17 constructs2^152 candidate quartets; this supports native quartet-storage scale, not bytes or128-bit blocks.

preprocessing.note: No separately reusable preprocessing resource is extracted from this attack.

success.description: Section6.2 expects16 right quartets before key ranking and sketches the final nine-byte completion. It gives no numerical full-key success. The Section6.1 trail/filters below are author models, not a validation of joint compatibility; the existing published probability-justification dispute is unchanged. This conference edition explicitly defers full ranking details to an extended version.

review.scope: Rechecked exact conference PDF8–17, including first-stage85-bit output, full-key completion, expected right-quartet counts, voting and the native AES192 failure/restart step. No numerical probability for the selected output at its listed native cost is established. Expected counts and local wrong-vote bounds do not fill this gap; published joint-probability, counting and memory disputes remain. Targeted endpoint success review, not a new full audit or attack reproduction.

components.description: PDF16: the source effective upper quantity is2^-(3*6+13)=2^-31. Section4 squares amplified upper/lower quantities when counting rectangle quartets; this is not full quartet or recovery success.
PDF16: four restricted output S-boxes contribute2^-24. This one-sided source quantity is squared in the quartet expectation, not itself a full success.
PDF16: the source rounds the switching-round effective contribution to2^(-6-2*3.5). The3.5 values describe amplified difference-collision quantities, not independent ordinary S-box transitions.
PDF16: the source ciphertext-difference set has35 bits of entropy among128 bits and is described as a93-bit filter; local wrong-quartet filtering only.
PDF17: the five-byte guess supplies a32-bit filtering step before the grouped key ranking. This conditional local sieve is not recovery probability.

Murphy explicitly questions the probability justification/data demand; subsequent authors continue to cite the proceedings budget. Neither fact proves a full-round zero-probability counterexample or validates the attack.

field_conflicts.label: Published probability-justification dispute
field_conflicts.description: Murphy explicitly questions the probability/data-demand justification of BK09. His concrete zero-probability AES example is a two-round single-key construction, not a counterexample to these full-round related-key trails. DEFN22 later continues to quote the historical BK09 estimates. Preserve the reported point with this dispute; neither automatic validation nor refutation is inferred.
